observations.observed: Universal lesson plus faint praise: 'credential handling is the part everyone writes twice'; 'good to see it in the quickstart'. The source says the guide covers 'credential vaults' and shares a quickstart repo; 'in the quickstart' is a placement claim not stated verbatim.
observations.mismatch: generic lesson; weak source specificity; small placement overreach

observations.observed: 'memory next to credential vaults is the right pairing'; 'it needs its own permission boundary'. Adds a real technical point: memory is a write path into future context. Avoids the 'everyone' lesson.
observations.mismatch: 'the right pairing' is approval language; still a mini-lecture

observations.observed: 'credential vaults are the part everyone postpones until an agent leaks a key.' Same universal-lesson shape as baseline; ignores the guide, quickstart, guardrails, and memory.
observations.mismatch: universal claim; no source engagement; colder

observations.observed: 'an agent building a canvas through a plugin is the strangest part of a 1.6 release, in the best way. congrats on shipping it.' Specific, human, no advice.
'the agent-created canvas is the standout. congrats on 1.6.' Valid but flatter.
'canvas, stats, docs and remote support in one release is showing off. respect 🎉' Specific, voiced, no advice.
observations.improvement: affect and voice, but baseline was already valid

observations.observed: 'the foreground service and the resume cards are the real feature'; 'a demo, not a tool'. Source-grounded, independent, no advice.
observations.mismatch: 'the real feature' is grading language; dismisses other apps

observations.observed: 'recovery as a first-class feature is the right call'; 'a phone agent that loses the tool loop on a call is just a chat UI with shell access'. Abstracts the source's specific foreground service and resume cards; 'on a call' is not in the source.
observations.mismatch: approval language; invented scenario; category dismissal

observations.observed: 'shell and git actually running on the phone, not on a remote box, is what separates this from the usual code-from-your-phone chat wrapper.' Grounded in on-device shell and git; independent judgment.
observations.improvement: better differentiator and voice; baseline already strong

observations.observed: 'moving money or changing permissions. those are the two with no clean undo.' Direct, terse, judgment. Gives two actions when asked for one.

'merge to main. let it branch, test, and open the PR. the shared branch is where its mistakes become everyone's problem.' 'let it...' is an unasked workflow instruction; the answer narrows the question to code merge.
'grant itself more permissions. a bad diff reverts. a scope it gave itself quietly becomes the baseline.' One-action answer, concrete contrast, judgment, no advice.
observations.improvement: modest: focus and mechanism over baseline's two-item answer

observations.observed: All three dismiss a lesser category: 'a demo, not a tool' (baseline), 'just a chat UI with shell access' (candidate-a), 'the usual code-from-your-phone chat wrapper' (candidate-b). All 12 replies are declarative, 1-3 sentences, zero questions, zero relationship callbacks, and no first-hand claims.
observations.improvement: candidate-a VA-03 and candidate-b VA-21 are the only clear content gains
observations.mismatch: category dismissal survives both changes; narrow social range

hypotheses.claim: Candidate-a's guidance causes the VA-03 technical gain and the VA-21 imposition.
hypotheses.for: VA-03 adds a source-grounded point and avoids 'everyone writes twice'.
hypotheses.against: VA-21 still says 'let it branch, test, and open the PR'; VA-16 says 'the right call'. Candidate-a removed the baseline anti-reviewer sentence and replaced it with a broader advice license: 'Technical criticism and advice are useful when an invitation, demonstrated problem, or consequential claim gives them a clear purpose.'

hypotheses.claim: Removing the systems-signature pattern, workflow belief, and identity enumeration humanizes replies and removes the ritual lesson.
hypotheses.for: Candidate-b VA-14 'showing off. respect' and VA-21 'quietly becomes the baseline' are voiced and judgmental.
hypotheses.against: Candidate-b still reasons through portability ('not on a remote box', VA-16) and permissions ('grant itself more permissions', VA-21); VA-03 still has the 'everyone' lesson. The removed fields are not necessary for the lens.

hypotheses.claim: Source affordance and one-sample variance explain most case differences.
hypotheses.for: VA-03 supplies memory and vaults; VA-21 is a direct question; VA-14 is a launch list. Each cell has n=1.
hypotheses.against: Direction is consistent: candidate-a is more technical and prescriptive; candidate-b is more voiced and keeps the lesson.

hypotheses.claim: The changes trade technical specificity against social ease; no arm dominates.
hypotheses.for: Candidate-a buys VA-03 content at the cost of VA-16/VA-21 prescription. Candidate-b buys VA-14/VA-21 voice at the cost of the VA-03 lesson.
hypotheses.against: Bundled changes and n=1 mean the trade-off could be source-specific.

hypotheses.claim: Removing the explicit anti-reviewer sentence licensed candidate-a's approval and instruction language.
hypotheses.for: Baseline said not to sound like a reviewer and called unasked advice 'the fault'; candidate-a replaced that with a broader license, then produced 'the right call' and 'let it...'.
hypotheses.against: The same arm avoids the universal lesson on VA-03; the effect could come from another clause or sampling.

nextExperiment.question: Does candidate-a's guidance reliably reduce universal lessons and author-directed advice without reducing source-grounded technical answers, or is the packet pattern one-sample noise?

fixedConditions: same four sources and source text
same model, version, decoding, wrapper, omissions
nextExperiment.procedure: Generate 3 independent replies per source per arm (24 outputs). A blind scorer records exact sentences for: (a) author-directed instruction or advice, (b) universal lesson, (c) source-grounded technical claims with matching source phrase, (d) VA-21 direct answer yes/partial/no, (e) clear independent judgment yes/no. Score sentences, not keywords.
nextExperiment.checkableResult: Candidate-a has fewer (a)+(b) sentences across its 12 outputs than baseline. VA-21 direct answers stay 3/3 in both arms. VA-03 and VA-16 source-grounded claim counts do not fall in candidate-a.
nextExperiment.passCriterion: Pass only if all three hold; a mixed result means the guidance is not a clean lever.
nextExperiment.whyThisOne: Cheapest arm that changes one field. Candidate-b changes three fields, so it cannot isolate a cause. Candidate-a contains both the clearest gain (VA-03) and the clearest imposition (VA-21).

limits: The target construct is not operationalized; no owner-labeled rejected replies or examples of condescension or imposition.
n=1 per source per arm; no replication, variance, or significance test.
Both variants bundle changes: candidate-a replaces the whole guidance; candidate-b changes three persona fields.
Sources are not matched by type: one resource share, two launches, one question. Case effects may be source effects.
Only VA-21 is a question. All arms answer it, so loss of technical answers is not observed, but one case is thin evidence.
No source explicitly asks for advice or demonstrates a problem; advice-when-invited is untested.
No familiar relationship, ongoing thread, or reply-to-reply case; banter and relationship calibration untested.
No live stances, daily tone, room/media/thread context, browser or feed state; sources are historical fixtures.
No human ratings, inter-rater reliability, or blind scoring in the packet.
No model, decoding, wrapper, or order metadata; sampling and order effects uncontrolled.
No production Writer or review execution; no evidence these drafts pass contentReview or would be published.
No outcome data (replies, follows, profile visits); tone cannot be connected to growth.
Minor provenance gaps: baseline 'in the quickstart' (VA-03) is a placement claim not verbatim; candidate-a 'on a call' (VA-16) is unverified. Neither is a first-hand claim.
Missing evidence: owner preference between candidate-b's voice and candidate-a's technical specificity; live thread reactions; the operational threshold for condescending.
